label: Ubiquiti EdgeSwitch 16 XP
description: Rackmount 1U chassis holding two EdgeSwitch 8XP systems: 16 gigabit RJ45 data ports with configurable passive PoE (off/24V/48V) on every data port, two 10/100 management ports (one per 8XP system) and a 300 W supply.
notes:
Census from Ubiquiti's own EdgeSwitch XP datasheet (https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgeSwitch_XP_DS.pdf, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 3,915,117 B, 7 pp, text layer, read 2026-11-21) and the tech-spec page (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/es-16xp, HTTP 200, 575,584 B, rendered table, same day).

**The chassis is two switches, not one.** p.1 names the models "ES-5XP, ES-8-XP, ES-16XP"; p.2 says the 16XP "features dual EdgeSwitch 8XP systems in a rack-mountable, 1U form factor with 300 watts of power supporting up to 16 devices"; p.7 prints "Hardware Configuration (2) EdgeSwitch 8XPs", 480 x 44.5 x 186 mm, 3.95 kg, 1U. p.4 lists "16 Gigabit PoE Ports". The per-port rows live on the ES-8XP page (p.6), which the tech-spec page heads with "* Specifications apply to each 8-Port EdgeSwitch ES-8XP unit": "Data Ports (8) 10/100/1000 Ethernet Ports", "Management Port (1) 10/100 Ethernet Port". Two units therefore expose 16 data ports and 2 management ports - which is why this entry now models eth1-eth16 plus mgmt0/mgmt1 instead of eight ports.

**What this entry got wrong until 2026-11-21:** it read the per-unit asterisk as a chassis fact and modelled eight data ports and one management port, recording the shortfall as a trap - "the model name says 16 XP but the sheet lists eight data ports". The sheet lists eight ports *per 8XP system*; the model name was right and half the switch was missing, so a lab could cable eight of its sixteen sockets and no more.

**PoE is passive and dual-voltage, not 802.3af/at.** p.6: "PoE Method Passive", "PoE Out Voltage Range 45-48VDC / 22-24VDC", "PoE Configurable Per Port: Management Port N/A, Data Ports Off/24V/48V", "Max PoE Wattage Per Data Port 11.5 W (24 V), 23 W (48V)". Ports are modelled at 11.5 W, the 24 V figure, because a port carries one voltage at a time and the engine bills one number per port; a port switched to 48 V can supply 23 W and the 300 W envelope (see the poe note) is what binds there. A standard 802.3af/at PD will not negotiate on any of these ports.

poe.note: 300 W is the datasheet's chassis figure, quoted not derived: p.2 "EdgeSwitch 16XP features dual EdgeSwitch 8XP systems in a rack-mountable, 1U form factor with 300 watts of power supporting up to 16 devices" and the p.4 feature list "16 Gigabit PoE Ports ... 300 W Power", against the per-unit "Max. Power Consumption 150 W" on the ES-8XP page (p.6). Ubiquiti does not print a row labelled "PoE budget" and does not say whether the chassis's own draw sits inside the 300 W, so this is an input envelope, not a measured budget: at 24 V (11.5 W a port) 16 ports total 184 W and all fit; at 48 V (23 W a port) 16 ports would be 368 W, so the supply, not the port count, is what stops a full 48 V fill. A lab that fits its own supply can state its own figure.
